title: Provider-authored agent definition
description: Validation contract for every file under agents/<DOMAIN>/. Keys marked catalog are copied into library_items.definition on publish; the rest is authoring metadata.

taskId.description: Project tracker id this agent implements.

model.description: Model id, and it must be one an enabled provider in the receiving workspace actually offers. There is no inheritance and no fallback: resolveForModel refuses a blank model rather than picking whichever provider happened to be first, because that would send a customer's data to a vendor they did not choose.

riskLevel.description: Blast radius if this agent acts wrongly, not how hard it was to build.

approvalRequired.description: True for anything that changes state. Drives the approval gate in core-service.

runtime.description: Runner the underlying automation needs. 'powershell' is currently blocked: job-service has no PowerShell runner or WinRM transport.

blockedBy.description: Present when this agent cannot run yet. Omit once runnable.

sourceScript.description: Relative path under Scripts/ whose param() block is the input contract. Null when greenfield.

instructions.description: The persona. PROVIDER-only: never serialised to a tenant caller.

tools.description: Closed allow-list. Referenced by stable ref, never numeric id.

ref.description: Stable key resolved to the tenant's delivered copy at rollout.

mutating.description: Whether running this changes the customer's state. ABSENT MEANS TRUE, on both sides of the wire: the phased runtime hides mutating tools from the phase that is still gathering evidence, and an unlabelled destructive automation must never be the one that slips through. Nothing else in the platform records this, so the agent's author declares it.

guardrails.description: Operational limits the persona must honour. Carried from the feasibility workbook where one exists.

then.description: PowerShell agents must declare why they cannot run yet.
Approval gates belong on state-changing agents; a read-only agent asking for approval is a mis-tagged definition.
